script.base: Market prices a low-scoring NE control game (implied NE 23.5 / TEN 17.0). New England leads by a score into the second half, leans Stevenson (29 car / 70 yds weeks 4-6) and Henderson (22/83) late, and does not need a shootout. Tennessee, a 6.5-point dog with Cam Ward at -0.16 EPA/db unblitzed and -0.54 vs the blitz, falls behind, trims the run, and throws short.
script.flip1: Home dog keeps it a one-score game all afternoon. Pollard keeps a full carry count (he just posted 64 and 67 rush yards), Ward never fully abandons the run, and NE cannot sit on Stevenson/Henderson. Pass-catcher overs still live, but the Pollard under dies.
script.flip2: NE jumps up two scores early. Starters' late pass snaps stall (Diggs/Boutte yards die), NE clocks out on the ground, and Tennessee's run share collapses so Pollard carries die while Okonkwo/Ayomanor checkdowns rise. A wind/rain slog is possible outdoors but the forecast was not saved.

Ayomanor's 224 air yards overlap NE's explosive allowance, but he has converted only 89 yards — overlap without efficiency.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and both lost. Okonkwo: Ward never sustains drives in a 17-point team total, the 4-yard floor shows up again, and Ridley's 14 targets die as incompletions to Ayomanor (224 air, 89 yards already) and Lockett (11 targets, 6 yards) instead of becoming Okonkwo catches; if Hawkins and Landry play, the middle is not as open as the 8.9 YPA split. Pollard: the game stays one score, he gets the 15-carry week that produced 64 and 67, Hance's backup holds up, and 4.34 YPC only has to fall a little to still clear 62.5. Worse, both numbers are unadjusted medians — the real market may already have moved, so this 'edge' may be a stale line we cannot see.
